title: Affine chart quotients form an open covering of an etale relation quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $V,R$ be schemes over $S$. Let $j=(s,t):R\to V\times_S V$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism such that for every $S$-scheme $T$, $j$ identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. Suppose $s,t$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] of the presheaf $T\mapsto V(T)/R(T)$, with quotient map $q:h_V\to F$, where $h_V(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,V)$. Choose a set-indexed affine open covering $V=\bigcup_{i\in I}V_i$; affine means isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for a commutative ring $A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $U=\coprod_{i\in I}V_i$ is a scheme, its summand inclusions are open and closed, and the canonical map $g:U\to V$ is surjective etale. Put $R_U=U\times_{g,V,s}R\times_{t,V,g}U$, and restrict $R_U$ along $V_i\to U$ to obtain $R_i\to V_i\times_S V_i$. These are etale equivalence relations. Write $Q=U/R_U$ and $F_i=V_i/R_i$ for the fppf sheafifications of the corresponding presheaf quotients. The canonical map $Q\to F$ is an isomorphism. Each composite $F_i\to Q\to F$ is a representable open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], meaning that its pullback by every $h_T\to F$ is represented by an open subscheme of $T$. The family $(F_i\to F)_{i\in I}$ covers $F$ as a sheaf: for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $x\in F(T)$ there is an fppf covering $\{T_\alpha\to T\}$ such that each restriction $x|_{T_\alpha}$ is the image of a section of some $F_{i(\alpha)}(T_\alpha)$. No algebraic-space hypothesis on $F$ or the $F_i$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the coproduct comparison isomorphism for Over.forget S to identify the underlying scheme of the actual coproduct in Over S with the scheme coproduct of the chosen charts. Its summand inclusions are open immersions. Their ranges are clopen: sigmaMk identifies them with the clopen summands of the topological disjoint union, and the comparison isomorphism preserves clopen sets. The Sigma.desc equations identify each inclusion followed by g with the corresponding chart map. The covering property of the chosen charts therefore proves g surjective, including the empty-index case.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), disjoint gluing specialization; spaces Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation), affine-coproduct paragraph

proof.text: Each $V_i\hookrightarrow V$ is an open immersion, hence etale. On the open cover of $U$ by its summands, the restriction of $g$ is precisely this morphism. The source-locality lemma therefore shows that $g$ is etale. In particular $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and its surjectivity from step 1 says that $\{g:U\to V\}$ is an fppf covering. This uses no quasi-compactness or finiteness of $I$.

Before quotient sheaves are supplied, prove the geometry of restriction directly. For an etale g:W→V, maps to the iterated pullback are triples (a,r,b) whose endpoints satisfy r≫s=a≫g and r≫t=b≫g. Thus the restricted relation is the inverse image of the original equivalence relation and is an equivalence relation on every test object. Equality of endpoints determines r by the original relation monomorphism and then the pullback universal properties determine the whole triple, proving monicity. Over.forget preserves the two pullback squares; base change and composition make their restricted projections etale. Apply this first to g and then to each summand inclusion. Once Q and its sheafification unit are supplied, apply the restriction-quotient theorem to g. The surjectivity established above makes its canonical quotient map β:Q→F an isomorphism, with the required quotient-projection equation.

source.place: Tag 02WT (lemma-pullback-etale-equivalence-relation); Groupoids Tag 045Z (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence-relation-restrict); Tag 02WW (theorem-presentation), replacement paragraph

proof.text: Apply the direct restricted-relation geometry argument from step 3 to the summand inclusion into the coproduct. This gives all four assertions for each chart relation before any chart quotient is chosen. The resulting iterated pullback is exactly the chartSource/chartTarget construction in the statement; no new quotient sheaf is chosen from an existence theorem.

Reflexivity supplies an $S$-morphism $e:U\to R_U$: apply the relation hypothesis on $U$-valued points to $(\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_U)$. Its two composites with the projections $s_U,t_U$ are $\mathrm{id}_U$. Hence $s_U,t_U$ are surjective on underlying points. Because $R_U$ is an etale equivalence relation, these projections are etale, so they are flat and locally of finite presentation by definition. The open immersion $\iota_i$ is etale by step 4, hence also flat and locally of finite presentation. These verify all hypotheses of the finding-opens lemma; no representability of $Q$ or $F_i$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), hypotheses (1)-(3), applied to the relation of Tag 02WT

proof.text: Apply finding-opens to the coproduct relation and every summand inclusion. This supplies a canonical map α_i:F_i→Q and its quotient-projection equation, together with representability by open immersions. For a map a:h_T→F, apply this assertion to a≫β⁻¹. Paste its pullback square with the pullback square defined by β and its inverse. This represents the pullback of α_i≫β by the same open immersion, proving the asserted representability.

Prove local chart lifting directly from the specified universal property, using the locally generated image construction of Sites 00WK in the same universe as the given sheaves. Put q=π≫η and let D be the subpresheaf of F whose sections are images of some chart quotient F_i. Its local closure E=D.sheafify is a subsheaf. Every q(v), for v:T→V, lies in E: pull the given open covering back along v; each member is an fppf cover arrow and has a map to its chart, whose quotient section maps to the restriction of q(v) by the compatibility equations. Hence q factors through E. The factor coequalizes s and t, since E→F is mono, and therefore descends to the presheaf coequalizer. The universal property hη gives l:F→E. Injectivity in the same universal property and epimorphy of π show l≫(E→F)=id_F. Thus every section of F lies in E, so its D-membership sieve is covering. The topology over S is generated by the comap of fppfPrecoverage along Over.forget S; the covering-sieve criterion extracts an actual fppf covering presieve inside this sieve. Its arrows have precisely the required chart quotient lifts. This handles empty and infinite chart index sets without a nonemptiness assumption.
